findings.quote: Dropping the denominator (1+n)² after finding the numerator 4n² leaves only 4n².
findings.note: The correct working in this solution has numerator 4n, not 4n², so "after finding the numerator 4n²" does not follow from any step printed above it; option 4 is only reached by first making the separate error described in common_mistakes[0] and then dropping the denominator. As written the entry describes no single error a student makes on this question.
findings.fix: Starting from the wrong energy fraction 4n²/(1+n)² of the previous entry and then dropping the denominator (1+n)² leaves only 4n².

notes: Own solve: m₂ = m₁/n, fraction transferred = 4m₁m₂/(m₁+m₂)² = 4n/(1+n)². Both other mistake entries verify exactly: (2m₁/(m₁+m₂))² = 4n²/(1+n)² (option 1) and 4m₁m₂/(m₁²+m₂²) = 4n/(1+n²) (option 3). The question itself never says the collision is elastic; the standard fraction formula and all four printed options presuppose it, and the solution states the assumption in its approach, which is the right handling.
